# Guest ABI

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-abi-doc.mjs — do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Sources: every Linker::func_wrap call in tension-core/src, and every
     Registration table in a capability adapter. -->

Every import a WebAssembly guest can call, grouped by module. These are the
only things the host offers: a guest that imports anything else fails at
instantiation, and that failure is the intended one.

85 imports across 12 modules: 52 registered by the host in 9 modules, 33 by 3 capability adapters.

A **capability** module is present only when its shared object is loaded
with `--capability`; the core modules are always present. Signatures are
written in WebAssembly value types, which is what a guest sees: a Rust
`u32` and a Rust `i32` are both `i32` here.

A module marked *core, and a capability on the bisect path* (`tension::2d`) is registered by the host in the default build, so it is always
present. The same ten imports are also the surface of a capability DSO,
built from `tension-2d/reference/` for a `--no-default-features` bisect;
the rows below carry that adapter's verb ids and flags, which the in-core
registration does not spell out.

This page states signatures, not errno contracts. An import that can refuse
says how in its own shim; the shared codes are in
[`adapter.md`](adapter.md#error-codes).

## Memory

| import | what it is | registered at |
|---|---|---|
| `env::memory` | the session arena, under both names the toolchains emit | `tension-core/src/session/mod.rs:485` |
| `session::memory` | the session arena, under both names the toolchains emit | `tension-core/src/session/mod.rs:488` |

`env::memory` and `session::memory` are the same memory: the session defines
it under both names so a guest built by either toolchain resolves it. A
guest without it is refused at load, not at the first call.
